Assert that a column only holds codes from a code list

Source: R/ensure_codes.R
ensure_codes.Rd

A checkpoint for coded columns: municipality, industry, education. A value outside the code list is a typo, an old code that should have been converted, or a code from another classification, and it silently drops out of every table built on the code list. On failure the offending rows are reported, with the codes counted. Returns data, so it can sit in the middle of a pipeline.

Usage

ensure_codes(
  data,
  column,
  codes,
  time = NULL,
  na_ok = TRUE,
  success_msg = NULL,
  warn_msg = NULL,
  abort_msg = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble, a database table (dbplyr, e.g. DuckDB) or an Arrow table or dataset; see Database and Arrow tables.

column

The coded column (tidy-select), e.g. municipality.

codes

A vector of valid codes, or a local data frame with columns code, valid_from, valid_to. An empty temporal list allows no codes.

time

Observation time column (tidy-select), required for a time-dependent code list and omitted for a vector.

na_ok

Whether a missing value passes. Default TRUE.

success_msg

Message shown when the rule holds. If NULL (default), it is "Check passed: <message>" when warn_msg or abort_msg is given, so the console names every check that ran, and a description of the check otherwise.

warn_msg

Message shown when values are outside the code list and no abort_msg is set. Defaults to a description of the check.

abort_msg

If provided, cli::cli_abort() is called with this message when the rule is broken. If NULL (default), a warning is issued instead.

Value

data invisibly, unchanged.

Details

Missing values pass by default, as missing is a different problem from a wrong code; set na_ok = FALSE to require a code on every row. The code list is compared as text when the column is text, so "0955" and "955" are different codes, as they are in the register.

For time-dependent codes, supply a data frame with code, valid_from and valid_to, and select the observation's time column. Boundaries are inclusive; missing boundaries are open. Multiple validity intervals per code are allowed. A non-missing code with missing time fails, since its validity cannot be established. na_ok only controls missing codes. Time and both boundaries must use the same scale: Date, POSIXct, or numeric periods. Years and dates are not implicitly mixed. The code list must have non-missing codes and ordered boundaries.

See also

describe_codes() for how codes change over periods, checkpoints.

Examples

persons <- data.frame(cpr = c("a", "b", "c", "d"),
                      municipality = c("955", "956", "95", NA))
valid <- c("955", "956", "957", "959", "960")
# "95" is not a municipality
ensure_codes(persons, municipality, valid)
#> Warning: Codes not in the code list: municipality
#> ℹ 1 row in 1 group:
#>     municipality cpr
#>     <chr>        <chr>
#>   1 95           c
